A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hyaline (eosinophilic) globules and vascular slit-like spaces of KS are the result of phagocytic and lysosomal activities of the neoplasm.

KS is a neoplasm of vascular endothelial cells that have phagocytic properties and that the hyaline (eosinophilic) globules (bodes) and vascular slits of KS are the phagocytic products and erythrophages, respectively, of the neoplasms.

KS is an intravascular neoplastic process with a high degree of erythrophagic activity, which is most likely the result of a combination of the increased fragility of the endothelial lining and the increased fragility and permeability of the red blood cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the intracellular erythrocytes in KS are not trapped within the vascular lumina, but are engulfed by the neoplastic spindle cells and are subsequently degraded by phagocytic and lysosomal activities.
the hyaline bodies of KS represent erythrophagocytes.
the hyaline bodies seen in light microscopy of Kaposi sarcoma are actually erythrophagocytes, which are red blood cells that have been phagocytised by the tumor cells.
